Just curious, how much can a horse carry?

I think 250 lbs is the absolute upper limit for anything that isn't a legit warhorse. Those chargers have to be strong to carry dudes in full plate armor. They are an equestrian team, so their horses are probably a lot smaller and definitely shouldn't be carrying whales on their backs.

The rule of thumb is 20% of its bodyweight, maximum. A horse's spine is a single piece from between its ears to the tip of its tail, so having it carry the proper weight is important, especially for sport. I don't know what breed OP's Duffy is, but your average riding horse is between 1,000 and 1,300 pounds. So 200-260 pounds, though most barns I've ridden at cap riders at 250 pounds, just to have a hard limit set.

Plus remember the saddle and tack weigh a bunch too.

So say, the horse can carry 200 pounds, and you have a 'light' 30 pound saddle, the horse shouldn't carry more than a 170 pound person.

For everything else, a horse should carry no more than 20% of their body weight on their backs. For the largest horse, this is about 250 lbs. Draft horses were not bred for riding, so their backs are a bit weaker and should only carry 15% of their weight, which works out to 300 lbs for the very largest draft horse.

These weights all include the weight of tack.
